data.name: Aamil
data.gender_notes: Aamil is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who does, creates, or works. The name Aamil carries the meaning “Worker, laborer, craftsman” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Aamil usually hope their child will grow to embody worker, laborer, craftsman and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Servant of Allah, devotee, seeker of knowledge
data.etymology: Aamil belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Worker, laborer, craftsman.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aamil total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Aamil" carries a strong cultural significance in the Islamic society, as it emphasizes the importance of productivity and action in various aspects of life. The Arabic root word 'A'mila' means 'to do' or 'to work', which is a fundamental concept valued in Islam. People with this name are often seen as dedicated and hardworking individuals who are motivated to achieve their goals and contribute positively to their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Aamil" serves as a reminder of our divine role as God's creatures to be active participants in our own lives and in the world around us. In Islamic teachings, every person is encouraged to strive for excellence and productivity in their religious, spiritual, and worldly pursuits. The name "Aamil" reflects this emphasis on personal accountability and active engagement with life, as well as the belief that every action, no matter how small, can have a profound impact on our noble character and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Worker, laborer, craftsman" symbolizes One who does, creates, or works. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Aamil serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of worker, laborer, craftsman.
